Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

contact verb

get in touch with

also get in touch, get in touch with, be in touch, keep in touch

classical

Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
Cic. Fam. 9.14.1: conveniō autem cotīdiē plūrimōs

conveniō, convenīre, convēnī, conventum

verb, fourth conjugation; transitive, convenīre aliquem

go and see, meet (to speak with)

Lewis & Short: “to go to one to speak to him, make a request of him, etc., to address, accost, meet, visit”. Latin names the way one gets in touch: in person convenīre, by letter or email scrībere ad aliquem, by messenger nūntium mittere, by phone tēlephōnicē colloquī (see talk on the phone).

Other words

  • scrībere ad aliquem — write to someone (a letter, an email)

    scrībō, scrībere, scrīpsī, scrīptum, with ad and the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 6.1.26: ergō id ipsum scrībēs ad mē

  • per litterās aut per nūntium certiōrem facere — let someone know by letter or by message

    certiōrem (certus), with faciō, facere, fēcī, factum; the person in the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 11.24.4: nē per litterās quidem aut per nūntium certiōrem facit mē

    See information.

Examples

  • Philotīmus nōn modo nūllus vēnit sed nē per litterās quidem aut per nūntium certiōrem facit mē quid ēgerit

    Philotimus hasn’t come at all, and hasn’t even been in touch by letter or by messenger to tell me what he has doneCic. Att. 11.24.4

  • itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus

    so far nobody who wanted to see me has found me busyCic. Sen. 32

See also message, information, talk on the phone, approach.
